postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_list_connection_profiles
postgresql.description: List all available PostgreSQL connection profiles. Returns a list of profiles with ID, name, host, port, and default database. Use the profile ID with postgres_mcp_connect to establish a connection.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_connect
postgresql.description: Connect to a PostgreSQL database server using a profile ID and optional database name. The profile ID is retrieved from postgres_mcp_list_connection_profiles. Returns a connection ID that is used to interact with the database with other tools from this postgres-mcp server. If a specific database is given and the connection fails, use postgres_mcp_list_databases against a connection to the default database to find the correct database name. The connection ID is a string formatted as 'postgres-mcp/{profile_id}[/{database name}]', where if no database name is present it's the default database for the profile.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_disconnect
postgresql.description: Disconnect from a PostgreSQL database server using a connection ID.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_list_databases
postgresql.description: List all databases on the connected PostgreSQL server. Requires a connectionId from postgres_mcp_connect. Returns a list of database names available on the server.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_db_context
postgresql.description:
Get context about this database by fetching the CREATE scripts for a specific type of database object or all types. Use this tool to retrieve detailed context about the database objects (e.g. tables, indexes, functions, sequences, comments, ownership, default_privileges, fdw, or all) within a given schema or across all schemas.
Note: Always call this tool first to fetch the most up-to-date database schema context before executing any queries or modifications. This tool is strictly read-only and prevents duplicate or conflicting operations by ensuring you know the current state.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_bulk_load_csv
postgresql.description:
Bulk‐load CSV file via COPY into a PostgreSQL table. Supports column mapping, optional SQL transforms, truncate-before-insert, and PK-based upsert. Use this to bulk-load CSV data into an existing table. The `path` must live under an approved bulk-load path (the current working directory by default, or one approved via `postgres-mcp allow-access-to-path <path>` / `POSTGRES_MCP_ALLOWED_PATHS`). A directory grants recursive access to descendants; a file grants access only to that exact canonical file.
Example:
postgres_mcp_bulk_load_csv(
    connectionId='postgres-mcp/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/mydb',
    path='/path/to/file.csv',
    table='mytable',
    mapping={'col1': 'col1', 'col2': 'col2'},
    transforms={'col2': 'src.col2::int'},
    mode='upsert'
)

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_describe_csv
postgresql.description: Describe the structure and contents of a CSV file. Returns a YAML description of the CSV file, including fields, types, and metadata. Useful for preparing to import CSV data into a database. The selected file path must be approved for CSV access (via `postgres-mcp allow-access-to-path <path>` or `POSTGRES_MCP_ALLOWED_PATHS`). A directory grants recursive access to descendants; a file grants access only to that exact canonical file.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_get_server_capabilities
postgresql.description: CALL THIS FIRST before diagnosing performance issues. Discovers what diagnostic tools are available for the connected server. Returns PostgreSQL version, Azure detection status, and available diagnostic groups for postgres_mcp_get_metrics_group. Each group includes its ID, description, and metric count. Shows why certain groups may be unavailable (missing extensions, version requirements, Azure-only features). Required step before using postgres_mcp_get_metrics_group for troubleshooting.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_get_metrics_group
postgresql.description: Diagnose slow database and performance issues. USE THIS FIRST when users report slow queries, high CPU, or performance problems. Collects pre-correlated metrics by diagnostic group: core_health (CPU, memory, connections, storage), saturation (I/O pressure, disk, cache performance), throughput (transactions, tuples, workload volume), lock_contention (blocking sessions, deadlocks, lock waits). For Azure servers, includes Azure Monitor metrics automatically. Call postgres_mcp_get_server_capabilities first to see available groups. Max 5 groups per request, max 7 days for historical data.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_query
postgresql.description: Run a formatted SQL query against a database. For performance diagnostics, prefer postgres_mcp_get_metrics_group instead. Requires a connection_id from the return value of postgres_mcp_connect. This query must not modify the database at all. Can include SELECT, SHOW, EXPLAIN etc. Do not include additional statements, e.g. SET search_path, in this query. It must only be a single, spacious, well formatted query with line breaks and tabs. The statement will be presented to the user, so focus on readability. Returns the results of the query. You MUST include a validation query to check the validity of EVERY literal value used in the SQL query. Do NOT skip this step. This tool is strictly read-only and executes a single statement only. Use EXPLAIN for performance or optimization analysis and include execution plan details. On error, return clear error messages to the user.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_modify
postgresql.description:
Modify the database and/or schema by executing SQL statements including DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) and DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). Useful when designing schemas or inserting data. It must only be a single, spacious, well formatted query with line breaks and tabs. The statement will be presented to the user, so focus on readability. Returns the results of the statement execution, if any.
Note: Always fetch up-to-date database schema context using the postgres_mcp_db_context tool before proposing or executing modifications to avoid duplicates or conflicts. Ensure explicit user confirmation. On error, return clear and descriptive error messages to the user. NOTE: Use this tool when working with PostgreSQL databases INSTEAD of asking the user to run the psql CLI tool, unless otherwise explicitly asked to.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_add_connection
postgresql.description: Add a new PostgreSQL connection profile. The profile will be stored in ~/.postgres-mcp/connections.yaml. IMPORTANT: This tool does NOT accept passwords for security reasons. After adding the connection, the user must run this in a new terminal, not in the Copilot session: `npx -y @microsoft/postgres-mcp connection set-password <profile_name>` to securely set the password via the OS keyring. For Docker/CI environments, use the POSTGRES_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable instead. Optionally set 'accessMode' to 'ro' (read-only) to block write tools (postgres_mcp_modify, postgres_mcp_bulk_load_csv) against this profile. Defaults to 'rw' (read-write) when omitted.

postgresql.name: postgres_mcp_remove_connection
postgresql.description: Remove a PostgreSQL connection profile. This removes the profile from ~/.postgres-mcp/connections.yaml and deletes its password from the OS keyring. Use postgres_mcp_list_connection_profiles to see available profiles.
